@dataclass(slots=True)
class RequestFl:
    """Request data files.

    Rules for valid filename.
    """

    filename: Path
    alphabet: str = field(
        default=ascii_lowercase + digits + '_áàãâéèêíìîóòõôúùûç', repr=False
    )
    considers_underscore: bool = field(default=True, repr=False)
    min_len: int = 3
    max_len: int = 256
    requires_audit: bool = False
    required_role: str | None = None
    action: str = ''
    audit_log: list[str] = field(default_factory=list[str], repr=False)
    code: Status = field(default=Status.SUCCESS, init=False)
    messages: list[str] = field(default_factory=list[str], repr=False)

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        """Post init."""
        self.filename = Path(self.filename)
        self.audit_log.append('')

    @property
    def refname(self) -> str:
        """Getting the reference name."""
        name = self.filename.stem
        regex = r'' if self.considers_underscore else '_'
        refname = re.sub(regex, '', name)
        ic(name, len(name), refname, len(refname), self.min_len, self.max_len)
        return refname

    @property
    def has_filename(self) -> bool:
        """Check if filename is null."""
        return bool(self.filename.name)

    @property
    def is_conf_test(self) -> bool:
        """Check if filename is conftest.py."""
        return bool(re.match(r'^conftest.py$', self.filename.name))

    @property
    def is_dundle_init(self) -> bool:
        """Check if filename is dundler init."""
        return bool(re.match(r'^__init__.py$', self.filename.name))

    @property
    def is_python_file(self) -> bool:
        """Check if python file."""
        return self.filename.suffix == '.py'

    @property
    def is_not_test_filename(self) -> bool:
        """Check if python not is a test file."""
        return bool(
            re.match(r'(?i)^(?:(?!tests?).)*$', self.filename.as_posix())
        )

    @property
    def has_test_pathname(self) -> bool:
        """Check if path is test."""
        return bool(re.match(r'^.*tests?.*$', self.filename.parent.as_posix()))

def add_class_method_decorator(
    method: Callable,  # type: ignore[type-arg]
    method_modo: Callable | None = classmethod,  # type: ignore[type-arg]
) -> Callable:  # type: ignore[type-arg]
    """Decorate dynamically add a class method into any class."""

    def wrapper(cls: Callable[..., Any]) -> Callable[..., Any]:
        """Wrap to add class method."""
        match method_modo:
            case Callable():
                setattr(cls, method.__name__, method_modo(method))
            case _:
                setattr(cls, method.__name__, method)
        logging.debug(dir(cls))
        return cls

    return wrapper

def backup_file(filename: Path, ext: str = '.bkp', start: int = 1) -> Path:
    """Backup file."""
    count = itertools.count(start=start)
    ext = f'.{ext.strip(".")}'
    bkp_dir = Path('.bkp')
    bkp_fl: Path = bkp_dir / f'{filename.stem}{filename.suffix}{ext}'

    bkp_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True, parents=True)

    while bkp_fl.is_file():
        bkp_fl = (
            bkp_dir / f'{filename.stem}{filename.suffix}{ext}.{next(count)}'
        )
    shutil.copy(filename, bkp_fl)

    return bkp_fl

def find_project_root(
    start_dir: Path | str = '', markers: tuple[str, ...] | None = None
) -> Path:
    """Find the project root directory by looking for specific markers."""
    ic(f'{inspect.stack()[0].function}: {start_dir=}, {markers=}')

    start_dir = Path(start_dir) if start_dir else Path.cwd()
    start_dir = start_dir.expanduser().resolve()
    start_dir = start_dir.parent if start_dir.is_file() else start_dir

    markers = markers or MARKERS[:]
    current = start_dir
    ic(f'{current=}, {markers=}')

    while current != current.parent:
        for marker in markers:
            if (current / marker).exists():
                ic(f'Found marker "{marker}" in {current}')
                return current
        current = current.parent

    msg = 'Project root not found (no markers detected).'
    ic(f'{msg} {start_dir=}, {markers=}')
    raise FileNotFoundError(msg)

def get_issue_from_branch() -> str:
    """Extrai o número do ticket do nome do branch."""
    # Obtém o nome do branch atual
    branch = (
        subprocess
        .check_output(['git', 'symbolic-ref', '--short', 'HEAD'])
        .strip()
        .decode('utf-8')
    )

    # Exemplo: branch '195-check-len-first' -> '195'
    match = re.match(r'^(\d+)\-.+$', branch)
    if match:
        return match.group(1)
    return ''  # Retorna string vazia se não houver correspondência

def get_signed_off_by() -> str:
    """Obtém a linha de assinatura 'Signed-off-by' do committer atual.

    Usa `git var GIT_COMMITTER_IDENT` para extrair o nome e email do committer.

    Returns:
        str: Linha formatada no padrão:
             "Signed-off-by: Nome <email>"

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: Se a execução do comando git falhar.

    """
    try:
        ident: str = subprocess.check_output(
            ['git', 'var', 'GIT_COMMITTER_IDENT'], text=True
        ).strip()
    except (
        subprocess.CalledProcessError
    ) as e:  # pragma: no cover; noqa: S110 TODO cover in future
        msg = 'Falha ao obter GIT_COMMITTER_IDENT'
        raise RuntimeError(msg) from e

    return f'Signed-off-by: {ident.split(">", maxsplit=1)[0]}>'

def logging_call(
    level: LoggingLevel = LoggingLevel.DEBUG, message: str = ''
) -> Callable[[Callable[P, R]], Callable[P, R]]:
    """Decoratore to debug function calls.

    Args:
      level::str: Level logging, default is debug;
      message::str: Message logging, default is ;

    """
    level = LoggingLevel(level)

    message = message or 'Function **{}** called.'

    def inner(func: Callable[P, R]) -> Callable[P, R]:
        """Inner funtion to receive parameters."""

        @wraps(func)
        def wrapper(*args: P.args, **kwargs: P.kwargs) -> R:
            """Wrapp function to add logging record."""
            debug: bool = debug_var_active()

            if debug:
                ic.enable()
                executable = (
                    f'Calling function: {func.__name__},',
                    f' Arguments: {args}, {kwargs}',
                )
                ic(executable)

            result = func(*args, **kwargs)

            getattr(logging, level.name.casefold())(
                message.format(func.__name__)
            )
            return result

        return wrapper

    return inner

def __extract_footers(content_lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """Extract the footer block (last non-empty paragraph).

    :param content_lines: commit message lines without comments.
    :return: lines of the last non-empty paragraph.

    .. versionadded:: 1.22.0
    """
    paragraphs: list[list[str]] = []
    current: list[str] = []
    for line in content_lines:
        if line.strip():
            current.append(line)
        elif current:
            paragraphs.append(current)
            current = []
    if current:
        paragraphs.append(current)

    return paragraphs[-1] if paragraphs else []

def __is_body_line(line: str) -> bool:
    """Check if a line is a plain body line (not a footer attempt).

    :param line: line of the last paragraph.
    :return: True se a linha e corpo livre (sem padrao de rodape).

def __is_footer_valid(file: Path) -> bool:
    """Check footers of a single commit message file.

    :param file: commit message file.
    :return: True se o rodape e valido; False caso contrario.

    .. versionadded:: 1.22.0
    """
    content_lines = [
        line
        for line in file.read_text(encoding='utf-8').splitlines()
        if not line.lstrip().startswith(LINE_COMMENT)
    ]
    footers: list[str] = __extract_footers(content_lines)

    for footer in footers:
        if __is_valid_footer(footer):
            logging.info('Valid footer: %s', footer)
            continue
        if __is_body_line(footer):
            continue
        logging.critical(
            'Invalid footer: %s'
            '\nExpected: <token>: <value> or <token> <value>,'
            ' tokens: %s; issue reference only in Closes/Refs.',
            footer,
            sorted(FOOTER_TOKENS),
        )
        return False

    return True

def __is_valid_footer(footer: str) -> bool:
    """Check a single footer line.

    :param footer: footer line.
    :return: True se o rodape e valido; False caso contrario.

    .. versionadded:: 1.22.0
    """
    match = re.match(
        r'^(?P<token>[A-Za-z-]+):\s*(?P<value>\S.*)$',
        footer,
    )
    if match:
        token: str = match.group('token')
        value: str = match.group('value')

        if token not in FOOTER_TOKENS:
            return False

        return not re.search(ISSUE_REFERENCE, value) or token in ISSUE_TOKENS

    # Forma especial de Conventional Commits: `Closes #<id>` / `Refs #<id>`.
    return bool(re.match(r'^(?:Closes|Refs) #\d+$', footer))

def check_commit_footer(filenames: list[str]) -> int:
    """Validate footers of commit message file(s).

    :param filenames: commit message files to validate.
    :return: 0 se todos os rodapes sao validos; 1 caso contrario.

    .. versionadded:: 1.22.0
    """
    status: int = 0
    for filename in filenames:
        file = Path(filename)
        if not file.is_file():
            logging.critical('File %s not found.', file)
            status = 1
            continue

        if not __is_footer_valid(file):
            status = 1

    return status

def clean_commit_msg(path: Path) -> bool:
    """Remove linhas do arquivo de commit.

    Entre:

    - A linha que começa com 'Please enter the commit message'
    - Até a linha contendo apenas '#'

    Cria um backup `.bkp` antes de sobrescrever.

    Args:
        path (Path): Caminho para o arquivo de mensagem de commit.

    Returns:
        True, se o arquivo foi modificado; caso contrário, False.

    """
    backup: Path = backup_file(path)

    shutil.copy(path, backup)

    result: list[str] = []
    skipping: bool = False
    changed: bool = False

    for line in path.read_text(encoding='utf-8').splitlines(keepends=True):
        if not skipping and line.lstrip().startswith(
            'Please enter the commit message'
        ):
            skipping = True
            changed = True
            continue
        if skipping and line.strip() == '#':
            skipping = False
            continue
        if not skipping:
            result.append(line)

    if changed:
        path.write_text(''.join(result), encoding='utf-8')
    return changed

    """Insere a saída do git diff.

    na primeira linha que começa com '#'
    dentro do arquivo de mensagem de commit.

    if not diff_output:

    lines = commit_msg_file.read_text(encoding='utf-8').splitlines(
        keepends=True
    )
    result = []

    for idx, line in enumerate(lines):
        if line.startswith('#'):
            # insere diff e interrompe após a primeira ocorrência
            result.append('\n' + diff_output + '\n')
            result.extend(lines[idx:])  # adiciona o resto sem perder conteúdo
            break
        result.append(line)
    else:
        # caso não exista linha começando com "#"
        result.extend(lines)

    commit_msg_file.write_text(''.join(result), encoding='utf-8')

def prefixing_commit_msg(commit_msg_filepath: Path | str) -> Result:
    """Automatically prefixing git commit messages.

    Explanation:
      This will match branch names like, this `feature/ISSUE-123` or `hotfix/ISSUE-1234`
      and prefixing `[ISSUE-123]` on message git commit, except in master, main, dev or tags.

    """
    commit_msg_filepath = Path(commit_msg_filepath)
    result = Result()

    branch = get_branchname()

    regex = r'(feature|hotfix)\/(\w+-\d+)'
    if re.match(regex, branch):
        issue = re.match(regex, branch).group(2)  # type: ignore[union-attr]
        with commit_msg_filepath.open('r+', encoding='utf-8') as fh:
            commit_msg = fh.read()
            fh.seek(0, 0)
            fh.write(f'[{issue}] {commit_msg}')
    elif branch not in {'master', 'dev', 'main', 'tags'}:
        result.message += '\nIncorrect branch name'
        result.code |= Status.FAILURE
    return result

@dataclass
class ValidateBranchname:
    """Rules for valid branch name."""

    msg_ok: str = '\nBranching name rules. [OK]'
    msg_refused: str = (
        '\nYour commit was rejected due to branching name '
        'incompatible with rules.'
        '{}'
    )
    violation_text: str = ''
    result: Result = field(default_factory=Result)
    branchname: str = field(default_factory=get_branchname)

    def asdict(self) -> dict[str, str | Result]:
        """Self dict."""
        return self.__dict__

    def __is_length_valid(self, branchname: str = '') -> bool:
        """Check if the branch name length is valid."""
        branchname = branchname or self.branchname
        regex: str = r'^[\w\d_-]{3,255}$'
        result = re.match(regex, branchname)

        if result:
            return True

        self.violation_text = (
            f'\n - Branch name "{branchname}" length is invalid.'
            ' Min 3 and Max 255 characters.'
        )
        return bool(result)

    def __is_branch_dev(self, branchname: str = '') -> bool:
        """Check if the branch name is a default branch."""
        branchname = branchname or self.branchname
        result = branchname in {ProtectedBranchName.DEV.value, 'development'}
        if result:
            self.violation_text = (
                f'\n - Branch name "{branchname}" is protected.'
            )
        return bool(result)

    def __is_branch_tags(self, branchname: str = '') -> bool:
        """Check if the branch name is a default branch."""
        branchname = branchname or self.branchname
        result = branchname == ProtectedBranchName.TAGS.value
        if result:
            self.violation_text = (
                f'\n - Branch name "{branchname}" is protected.'
            )
        return bool(result)

    def __is_branch_main(self, branchname: str = '') -> bool:
        """Check if the branch name is main branch."""
        branchname = branchname or self.branchname
        result = branchname in {
            ProtectedBranchName.MAIN.value,
            ProtectedBranchName.MASTER.value,
        }
        if result:
            self.violation_text = (
                f'\n - Branch name "{branchname}" is protected.'
            )
        return result

    def __is_refused(self, branchname: str = '') -> bool:
        """Check if the branch name is refused."""
        branchname = branchname or self.branchname
        regex: str = RULE_BRANCHNAME_REFUSED
        result = re.match(regex, branchname, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
        ic(result)
        if result:
            self.violation_text = '\n - Can not be WIP (Work in Progress)'
        return bool(result)

    def __is_github_branch(self, branchname: str = '') -> bool:
        """Check if the branchname is a GitHub rule."""
        branchname = branchname or self.branchname
        regex_github = r'^\d+(-[\w_]{3,})+'

        return bool(re.match(regex_github, branchname))

    def __is_enhancement_epoch(self, branchname: str = '') -> bool:
        """Check if the branchname is enhancement-<epoch-timestamp>."""
        branchname = branchname or self.branchname
        regex_enhancement = r'^enhancement-\d{1,11}$'

        return bool(re.match(regex_enhancement, branchname))

    def __is_incolume_branch_rule(self, branchname: str = '') -> bool:
        """Check if the branchname is incolume rule."""
        branchname = branchname or self.branchname
        regex_incolume = (
            rf'^({"|".join(TypeCommit.to_set())})/(epoch|issue)#([0-9]+)$'
        )

        return bool(re.match(regex_incolume, branchname))

    def __is_not_matches_rule(self, branchname: str = '') -> bool:
        """Check if the branch name matches the rule."""
        branchname = branchname or self.branchname
        if not bool(re.match(RULE_BRANCHNAME, branchname)):
            self.violation_text = (
                '\n\n:: These syntaxes are allowed for branchname:'
                "\n - #1: 'enhancement-<epoch-timestamp>'; or"
                "\n - #2: '<issue-id>-issue-description'; or"
                "\n - #3: '<(feature|feat|bug|bugfix|fix)>/issue#<issue-id>'; or"
                "\n - #4: '<(feature|feat|bug|bugfix|fix)>/epoch#<epoch-timestamp>'"
            )
            return True
        return False

    def is_valid(self, branchname: str = '', **kwargs: str) -> Result:
        """Validate branch name.

        Args:
          branchname (str, Active branch): Branch name to validate.

          kwargs:
            protected_dev (bool, False): Consider dev as protected branch.
            protected_tags (bool, False): Consider tags as protected branch.
            protected_main (bool, True): Consider main/master as protected branch.

        Returns:
            int: Status code.

        """
        branchname = branchname or kwargs.get('branchname') or self.branchname
        protected_dev = kwargs.get('protected_dev', False)
        protected_tags = kwargs.get('protected_tags', False)
        protected_main = kwargs.get('protected_main', True)

        logging.debug('detected: %s', ic(branchname))
        logging.debug('protected dev: %s', ic(protected_dev))
        logging.debug('protected tags: %s', ic(protected_tags))
        logging.debug('protected main/master: %s', ic(protected_main))

        ic(self.result)
        msg: str = ''

        if protected_main and self.__is_branch_main(branchname):
            ic('is main protected branches')
            self.result.code = Status.FAILURE
            msg += self.violation_text

        if protected_dev and self.__is_branch_dev(branchname):
            ic('is dev protected branches')
            self.result.code = Status.FAILURE
            msg += self.violation_text

        if protected_tags and self.__is_branch_tags(branchname):
            ic('is tags protected branches')
            self.result.code = Status.FAILURE
            msg += self.violation_text

        if self.__is_refused(branchname):
            ic('is refused branch')
            self.result.code = Status.FAILURE
            msg += self.violation_text

        if self.__is_not_matches_rule(branchname):
            ic('is not matches rule')
            self.result.code = Status.FAILURE
            msg += self.violation_text

        if self.result.code == Status.FAILURE:
            self.result.message = self.msg_refused.format(msg)
        else:
            self.result.message = self.msg_ok

        return self.result

def validate_filename(
    filename: str, **kwargs: dict[str, str | Path]
) -> RequestFl:
    """Check if a filename is valid.

    A valid filename is in snake_case and has at least `min_len` characters.
    extract the name so that `/my/repo/x.py` becomes `x`

    Args:
      filename (Path | str): Filename to check;
      kwargs:
        min_len (int): Minimum length of the filename (default: 3);
        max_len (int): Maximum length of the filename (default: 256);
        considers_underscore (bool): If consider
              underscore in filename (default: True);

    Returns:
        Result: The result of the check.

    Examples:
        >> validate_filename('module/valid_name.py')
        RequestFl(filename=WindowsPath('module/valid_name.py'), min_len=3, max_len=256, requires_audit=False, required_role=None, action='rule_has_filename_ends_with_test', code=<Status.SUCCESS: 0>)

    """  # ruff:ignore[line-too-long]
    flname: Path = Path(filename or kwargs.get('filename', ''))  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    min_len = kwargs.get('min_len', 3)
    max_len = kwargs.get('max_len', 256)
    considers_underscore = kwargs.get('considers_underscore', True)
    request: RequestFl = RequestFl(
        flname,
        min_len=min_len,
        max_len=max_len,
        considers_underscore=considers_underscore,
    )

    policies: list[PolicyFn] = [
        rule_filename_notnull,
        rule_snake_case,
        rule_length,
        rule_not_started_with_number,
        rule_has_filename_ends_with_test,
    ]

    request = rule_filename_structure(request)
    if not request.is_python_file and request.code is Status.SUCCESS:
        return request

    request = apply_policies(request, policies)
    logging.debug(request)

    return request

@logging_call(logging.INFO, 'Validating commit message format.')
def validate_format_commit_msg_cli(
    ctx: click.Context,
    **kwargs: dict[str, Any],
) -> int:
    """Validate commit message.

    Hook designed for stages: prepare-commit-msg, manual
    """
    logging.warning(
        'callable=%s, command=%s, ctx.params=%s, kwargs=%s',
        inspect.stack()[0].function,
        ctx.command_path,
        ctx.params,
        kwargs,
    )
    ctx.params.update(kwargs)

    nonexequi = ctx.params.get('nonexequi')
    filenames = ctx.params.get('filenames')

    if nonexequi:
        click.secho(
            'Hook not executed due to the `--nonexequi` option.',
            fg='yellow',
        )
        ctx.exit(0)

    result: Result = validate_format_commit_msg(filenames=filenames)

    click.secho(
        result.message, fg='green' if result.code == Status.SUCCESS else 'red'
    )
    ctx.exit(result.code.value)

docs.title: Referência do CLI
docs.text: O grupo githooks-cli agrega todos os comandos do pacote; cada um também é publicado como entry-point em [project.scripts] do pyproject.toml, consumível diretamente pelo pre-commit.

docs.title: Comandos
docs.text: comando função githooks-cli grupo chain com todos os comandos check-commit-footer valida os rodapés do último parágrafo da mensagem check-len-first-line valida o comprimento da primeira linha da mensagem check-type-commit-msg valida o tipo da mensagem (Conventional Commits) clean-commit-msg limpa o arquivo de mensagem de commit detect-key detecta chaves privadas nos arquivos informados effort-msg exibe mensagem de esforço pós-commit effort-random-msg exibe mensagem de esforço aleatória (--fixed fixa a mensagem) insert-diff-commit insere o git diff --cached na mensagem de commit is-precommit-installed verifica se o pre-commit está instalado is-valid-branchname valida o nome da branch atual is-valid-filename valida nomes de arquivo Python is-valid-msg-commit valida o formato da mensagem de commit set-footer-signed-off-by insere rodapé Signed-off-by set-issue-from-branch extrai a issue do nome da branch para a mensagem

docs.title: Opções
docs.text:
• -N / --nonexequi — presente em todos os comandos: reporta que o hook não executou devido à opção.
  • -V / --version — versão do pacote.
  • -h / --help — ajuda do comando.

docs.title: Uso dos hooks
docs.text: Os hooks são o contrato público deste pacote com o pre-commit; os ids abaixo vêm do arquivo .pre-commit-hooks.yaml, que é a fonte de verdade. Mudança de nome, id ou argumento é quebra de API.

docs.title: Lista de hooks
docs.text: id entry stages função check-commit-footer check-commit-footer commit-msg, manual valida os rodapés do último parágrafo da mensagem de commit (Closes, Refs, Signed-off-by, Co-authored-by, Reviewed-by, Acked-by; referência #<id> só em Closes/Refs) check-len-first-line check-len-first-line prepare-commit-msg valida o comprimento da primeira linha da mensagem de commit check-precommit-installed is-precommit-installed pre-commit, pre-push garante que o pre-commit está instalado no projeto check-valid-branchname is-valid-branchname pre-commit, pre-push valida o nome da branch atual (protegidas e padrões válidos) check-valid-filenames is-valid-filename pre-commit, pre-push valida nomes de arquivo Python (snake_case, comprimento, localização de testes) clean-commit-message clean-commit-msg prepare-commit-msg limpa o arquivo de mensagem de commit detect-key detect-key commit detecta a presença de chaves privadas nos arquivos staged effort-message effort-msg post-commit exibe mensagem de esforço/motivação após o commit effort-random-message effort-random-msg post-commit exibe mensagem de esforço aleatória após o commit footer-signed-off-by set-footer-signed-off-by prepare-commit-msg insere rodapé Signed-off-by via git interpret-trailers insert-diff-commit insert-diff-commit prepare-commit-msg insere o git diff --cached na mensagem de commit validate-message-commit is-valid-msg-commit pre-commit, pre-push valida o formato da mensagem de commit (Conventional Commits) set_issue_from_branch_cli set-issue-from-branch prepare-commit-msg extrai o número da issue do nome da branch e insere na mensagem

docs.title: Argumentos comuns
docs.text:
Todos os comandos aceitam:

  • -N / --nonexequi — não executa o hook (o hook informa que não rodou devido à opção).
  • -V / --version — versão do pacote.

Hooks check-valid-filenames e check-len-first-line também aceitam limites configuráveis (ex.: --min-len, --max-len, --min-first-line, --max-first-line).

docs.title: Modelo completo
docs.text: O modelo de .pre-commit-config.yaml pronto para copiar está no README — ele é a fonte publicada para projetos consumidores.

docs.title: Instalação
docs.text: O consumo do pacote se dá, em geral, pelo pre-commit no projeto consumidor — o pacote não precisa ser instalado diretamente na maioria dos casos.

docs.title: Via pre-commit (recomendado)
docs.text:
Adicione ao .pre-commit-config.yaml do projeto consumidor:

- repo: https://github.com/development-incolume/incolume.py.githooks
  rev: 1.20.0
  hooks:
    - id: check-len-first-line
    - id: detect-key
    # demais hooks: consulte o modelo no README

Revisão publicada

A rev citada acima deve refletir a última tag publicada; o modelo completo e atualizado está no README do repositório.

docs.title: Via pip/uv (a partir do repositório)
docs.text:
pip install git+https://github.com/development-incolume/incolume.py.githooks.git

uv tool install git+https://github.com/development-incolume/incolume.py.githooks.git
